segment.description: Conasauga River (GNIS 00327507), Coosa-basin drainage — restricted to the TENNESSEE reaches the catalog entry covers. TDEC designates the Tennessee reach as a State Scenic River: 'The entire segment of the river in Polk County, upstream from the Highway 411 bridge', Class I Natural River Area, designated April 23, 1969, ~10.1 miles, one of only two Tennessee Scenic Rivers in the Cherokee National Forest. The river crosses the TN/GA line more than once near Tennga; the famous rare-species research (Conasauga logperch, amber darter, listed mussels) and Georgia's 2015 Outstanding National Resource Water designation apply to the GEORGIA reaches (Cohutta Wilderness headwaters, Jacks River) and are NOT attributed to the Tennessee reach here.
segment.boundaries: Polk County segments of the river upstream of the US-411 bridge (take-out 35.00888, -84.73389, at the state line near Tennga) per the TDEC Scenic Rivers designation; the USGS gauge 02384000 'CONASAUGA RIVER AT US 411, NEAR TENNGA' (35.0095, -84.7338, 108 sq mi — listed under Polk County TN, operated by the USGS Georgia center) sits at the downstream boundary of this reach.

coldSource.notes: Freestone river draining the Cohutta Mountains through the Cherokee National Forest; the Tennessee scenic segment is a narrow valley run with Class II-III rapids per TDEC's paddling description. No dam, no spring-influence documentation for the TN reach. Gauge altitude at the US-411 boundary is ~756 ft (USGS 02384000), so the TN reach is low-elevation; no agency statement on TN-reach summer cold-water refuge was located.

holdover.detail: No trout presence of any kind documented for the Tennessee reach — no stocking program rows, no trout designation, no creel or angler documentation located — so holdover cannot be assessed.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented in the Tennessee reach. TDEC's Scenic River page describes a rich native fish community — 'more than 90 fish species and 25 mussel species' with federal and state-listed aquatic species — and names no trout. The celebrated rare-fish work and any trout headwater fishery (Cohutta Wilderness, Jacks River, GA's 2015 ONRW designation) are on the Georgia reaches and do not transfer to the TN reach. TWRA's stocking workbook contains zero Conasauga rows, and the river is absent from TWRA's wild-trout/special-regulation lists.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The only summer data for the Tennessee reach — USGS grabs at the US-411 state-line crossing bounding it — read 20.0-24.0 degC (1957-1996), marginal for trout, and no source documents any trout presence, stocking, or fishery on the TN reach itself.
